title: Ranveer Just Bet ₹300 Crore on Zombies. Vicky Just Blocked 18 Months for Gods. Welcome to Bollywood's Biggest Genre Gamble.
excerpt: Two of India's most magnetic leading men are about to go where Hindi cinema has never been — one to a post-apocalyptic Mumbai, the other to a mythological battlefield. And they're bringing the South's biggest names with them.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ranveer Singh bets ₹300 crore on *Pralay*, a post-apocalyptic zombie thriller.
  • Vicky Kaushal blocks 18 months for *Mahavatar*, a mythological epic set for Christmas 2026.
  • Both films aim to redefine Hindi cinema with high budgets and international production teams.
  • Casting includes Kalyani Priyadarshan and potential pairing of Vicky with Deepika Padukone.
  • These projects signal Bollywood's ambition to compete with Hollywood standards.

Here's what Bollywood's two most bankable leading men are doing with all that clout: something genuinely terrifying. **Ranveer Singh**, fresh off the ₹1,300-crore rampage of *Dhurandhar*, is gambling big on *Pralay* — a ₹300-crore post-apocalyptic zombie thriller set in a devastated version of Mumbai. **Vicky Kaushal** has blocked eighteen full months of his calendar for *Mahavatar*, a mythological epic from **Amar Kaushik** — the man behind *Stree* and *Bala* — set to land in theatres this Christmas. And both films have just started making casting moves that suggest these aren't vanity projects. They're swings at redefining what Hindi cinema can do. https://youtube.com/watch?v=FBKcTzYVadI ![Vicky Kaushal — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/14/Vicky_Kaushal_snapped_promoting_Zara_Hatke_Zara_Bach_Ke_on_the_sets_of_The_Kapil_Sharma_Show_%28cropped%29.jpg) ## The Zombie Film Bollywood Never Made > **"At ₹300 crore, *Pralay* will be among the most expensive Hindi films ever produced, with a major chunk of filming set in Australia under the supervision of international technicians."** *Pralay* is not an action film that happens to have zombies in it. It is, by every account, a full-commitment genre picture — the kind India has watched from Hollywood but never attempted at this scale. Directed by **Jai Mehta**, who co-directed *Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story* and the Prime Video series *Lootere*, the film follows a married couple fighting to survive in a post-apocalyptic Mumbai. The tone, insiders say, lives somewhere between *World War Z* and *I Am Legend* — big-canvas survival cinema where the human story carries the spectacle. The budget reflects the ambition. At ₹300 crore, *Pralay* will be among the most expensive Hindi films ever produced, with a major chunk of filming set in Australia under the supervision of international technicians. Pre-production is already rolling, and principal photography begins in September. ![Amar Kaushik — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/98/The_Director_Amar_Khaushik_of_the_film_AABA%2C_at_the_Presentation%2C_during_the_48th_International_Film_Festival_of_India_%28IFFI-2017%29%2C_in_Panaji%2C_Goa_on_November_27%2C_2017.jpg) And the casting is just as bold. Ranveer personally called **Kalyani Priyadarshan** — the South Indian sensation whose fantasy thriller *Lokah* grossed ₹303 crore worldwide — to play the female lead. Kalyani was reportedly hesitant to make her Bollywood debut in a genre this niche, but Ranveer, who is also producing the film under his new banner **Maa Kasam Films**, spent considerable time walking her through the script's vision and the ambitious scale of the production. She said yes. That pairing — the man who carried *Dhurandhar* and the woman who made *Lokah* a phenomenon — is designed to make *Pralay* play across every language market, not just the Hindi belt. The co-production team reads like a prestige play: **Hansal Mehta's True Story Films** and **Sameer Nair's Applause Entertainment** are on board, with the screenplay by Jai Mehta and *Lootere* writer **Vishal Kapoor**.
Casting Moves in Bollywood
›Kalyani Priyadarshan cast as female lead in *Pralay*.
›Deepika Padukone in talks for *Mahavatar*.
›Ranveer Singh producing *Pralay* under Maa Kasam Films.
›Amar Kaushik directs *Mahavatar*, known for *Stree*.
## The Mythology Film That Demands 18 Months![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg) Then there is *Mahavatar*. Where *Pralay* is dystopian and dark, *Mahavatar* is ancient and divine — and the scale it demands is the reason Vicky Kaushal has reportedly locked his schedule for a year and a half. Directed by Amar Kaushik, whose *Stree* franchise turned folk-horror into a billion-rupee business, *Mahavatar* takes on Indian mythology at a scale meant to rival anything Hollywood has done with Greek or Norse gods. Details are guarded, but what's leaking out is mouthwatering. The film arrives in theatres on **December 23, 2026** — a Christmas release that signals pure commercial confidence. And the latest whisper from the trade? **Deepika Padukone** is in talks to star opposite Vicky as the female lead. If it happens — and sources suggest discussions are still in their early stages — it would be the first time Deepika and Vicky have shared a frame. That pairing alone is worth the price of a ticket. ## Why This Matters for the Diaspora For NRIs watching from New York, Toronto, and London, this is the clearest sign yet that Bollywood is finally building the kinds of films that don't need an asterisk. Not "good for Bollywood." Not "entertaining but ignore the VFX." Both *Pralay* and *Mahavatar* are being mounted with the kind of budgets, technical infrastructure, and international production teams that put them in direct conversation with Hollywood tentpoles. *Pralay* films in Australia with VFX pipelines built for global standards. *Mahavatar* carries the mythological storytelling India invented — reimagined for an audience that grew up on Marvel. These are films designed to play in IMAX screens in New Jersey and multiplexes in Mumbai alike. It is the boldest second half any Bollywood year has promised in recent memory. And the two men at the centre of it — one bouncing with feral energy, the other radiating quiet intensity — have never been more interesting to watch.
